No automatic motion replay or reconnect/re-enable
Preserve first failure and any separate cleanup-stop outcome
The existing campaign may issue its explicitly planned separate stop only while its stream and native prerequisites permit it

execution: Use existing scripts/s2_bench_console.py in one serial session; retain its exact command line and raw bytes
Select physical interface host 0 and useaddr N, with tracing off and no retained public operation
Send the explicit TB arming line, then debug raw and the public velocity command immediately after CONSOLE armed, within the existing freshness bound
Do not put debug raw before TB: the existing console-hold guard deliberately rejects T routes while tracing
After a successful terminal, debug off, release the bench record r, and retain a fixed six-second output tail
Copy and release the separate public operation using its actual admitted operation ID; r releases only the bench record
A refusal stops the helper's later steps; inspect it before separate trace cleanup or release
runner_limits: The ordinary motion campaign's handshake can consume TB freshness and its unchanged 64 KiB command-input guard cannot cover worst-case all-kind motion traces. Use the existing immediate shared-console helper for this experiment; ordinary runners are qualified separately by read campaigns. Four-second observation intervals keep the conservative two-cycle stop budget within the fixed ten-second settlement tail. Do not weaken either guard.
capture: Raw diagnostics with explicit off/drain and loss counters, typed results, host and firmware processing times, image identity and resource counters. Audit TX/RX pairs separately. No exact physical arrival timestamps.
